THESE APPEALS AND CROSS OBJECTIONS COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT The Manager vs Sharanappa And Ors on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56338490/
6
Though matters are listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, they are taken-up for final disposal.

2. Challenging common judgment and separate awards dated 11.01.2022 passed by Member, Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal No.IX, Vijayapur, (for short, 'Tribunal') in MVC no.442/2019 and MVC NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 no.584/2019, these appeals are filed by Insurer.

entities.text: Motor Vehicle Accident Claims Tribunal No.IX, Vijayapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In appeals respective claimants have filed cross-objections for enhancement.

2. Shri Manvendra Reddy, learned counsel for appellant/Insurer submitted that in an accident that occurred on 13.12.2018, Santhosh and Umesh stated to be rider and pillion rider of motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-28/EN-3587 traveling from Kolhar to Telagi sustained fatal injuries,
when a light goods vehicle bearing registration no.KA-28/C-5750 allegedly driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner dashed against motorcycle.
Separate claim petitions were filed by legal representatives of deceased against owner and insurer of light goods vehicle under Section 166 of Motor vehicles Act.
Owner though served did not file objection.
Insurer opposed claim petition on all counts.
Contributory negligence against rider of motorcycle and violation of terms and condition of policy by insured were also alleged.
Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and thereafter recorded evidence of NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 claimants in both appeal as PWs.1 and 2, eyewitness as PW.3, Ex.

P.1 to Ex.P.7 were got marked while insurer got marked copy of Insurance Policy, 'B'
register extract and driving licence of driver of respondent no.1 with consent as Ex.R1 to Ex.R3.
3.

On consideration, Tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of light goods vehicle by its driver, vehicle was insured with insurer and therefore insurer was liable to pay compensation.
It assessed compensation at `12,99,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and held insurer liable to pay same.

However, at time of passing award, contention of insurer about contributory negligence between two vehicles involved as well as contention of insurer regarding violation of terms and conditions of policy insofar as non- possession of fitness certificate in respect of insured vehicle as on date of accident were not considered and therefore seeks for allowing appeals by modifying award in view of said contentions.

Sri Sanganagouda Biradar, learned counsel for cross-objectors/claimants, submitted that rider and pillion rider were aged 18 and 19 years respectively, earning `25,000/- per month each from milk vending, died due to accidental injuries.

It was submitted that Tribunal considered their monthly income at meager extent of `11,750/-.
5.

It was further submitted that Tribunal erred in not adding future prospects and even award under conventional heads was not in accordance with decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1 and sought for enhancement of compensation.

7 6.
Heard learned counsel.
Perused impugned judgment and award and copies of deposition and exhibits made available by learned counsel for appellant/Insurer.
From above submission, occurrence of accident, involving of insured vehicle and death of rider and pillion rider of motorcycle in said accident are not in dispute.

While insurer is in appeal challenging finding of Tribunal on contributory negligence as well as finding regarding liability of insurer, cross-objectors/claimants are seeking for enhancement of compensation.

Therefore, points that arise for consideration in these appeals/cross objections are - "i) Whether Tribunal was justified in holding entire negligence against driver and insured light goods vehicle ?
ii) Whether Tribunal committed error in fastening liability upon insurer when there was violation of condition of policy ?
iii) Whether cross-objectors / claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for ?"
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 8.

Point no.(i) : In order to establish negligence against driver of insured vehicle, claimants relied on FIR, Complaint, Spot Mahazar, Motor Vehicle Inspector's report and Charge-sheet got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P.4 and Ex.P.6 respectively.
Complaint is registered against driver of insured light goods vehicle for offences under Sections 279, 338 and 304A of Indian Penal Code read with Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Ex . P.6 - charge- sheet also indicates that driver of insured vehicle was prosecuted for above mentioned offences apart from Sections 181, 187 and 3 of Motor Vehicles Act.
Ex.P.4 - Motor Vehicle Inspector's report would indicate that damages sustained by both vehicles were on their front side.
9. It is seen that accident occurred on a 22 feet wide road running north-south road.
But claimants have examined eyewitness as PW.3, who deposed that at accident spot, driver of light goods vehicles took vehicle on wrong side and dashed against motorcycle.
In cross- - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 examination except making suggestions about witness not having witnessed accident, there is no serious dispute about negligence.

Since police after investigation have filed charge-sheet against driver of insured vehicle for rash and negligent driving and causing of accident,
The Manager vs Sharanappa And Ors on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56338490/
8 finding of Tribunal regarding negligence would not call for interference.

8

sentences.text: Point no.(i) is answered in negative.
10. Point no.(ii) : Ex.R2- 'B' register extract would indicate that fitness certificate issued in respect of vehicle was valid upto 31.08.2018.
The certificate was issued on 19.07.2019.
The accident occurred on 13.12.2018.
There is no reference in certificate about vehicle being subsequently certified fit.
Non-possession of fitness certificate would be in violation of terms and conditions of policy.
However, claimants in instant case are riders of motorcycle i.e., third parties, insofar as insurer herein is concerned.

Therefore, as held by Division Bench of this - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 Court in Mr.Rajesh Poojary v/s Mr.Rajesh2 and Full Bench in case of New India Assurance Company Limited v/s Yallavva and another3, non-possession of fitness certificate would not be a fundamental breach of terms and conditions of policy.

entities.text: New India Assurance Company Limited v/s Yallavva and another3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, insurer would be liable to pay compensation to claimants in first instance and thereafter recover same from insured.
Consequently, point no.(ii) is answered partly affirmative.
11. Point no.(iii):

Insofar as claim for enhancement of compensation, in MVC no.442/2019 deceased Santhosh was aged 20 years and earning `25,000/- per month from milk vending, but same is not substantiated with specific evidence.
In absence, Tribunal assessed it notionally at `11,750/-.
However, Tribunal has not added future prospects.

Claimants are parents and unmarried younger siblings, though they are stated to be dependant on deceased, in absence of specific evidence regarding dependency, Tribunal has deducted one half 2019 SCC OnLine KAR 3005 ILR 2020 KAR 2341 - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 towards personal expenses and applied multiplier of '18' which is proper.
As deceased was aged below 40 years and self employed, future prospects at 40% has to be added to his income.

Thus, loss of dependency would be :
`11,750/- + 40% X 12 X 18 X 50% =`17,76,600/-.
12.
In addition, claimants would be entitled to compensation of `40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and `15,000/- towards loss of estate and `15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
Since more than three years have lapsed they would be also entitled for addition of 10% under conventional heads i.e., `11,000/-.
Thus, total compensation would be `18,97,600/-.
Point no.(iii)
answered partly affirmative as above.
13. In MVC no.584/2019 also claimants are parents and younger siblings.
For want of specific evidence regarding dependency, Tribunal deducted 50% towards personal expenses and applied multiplier of '18' and considered monthly income at `11,750/-.

Therefore, claim The Manager vs Sharanappa And Ors on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56338490/
9 - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 is virtually same as in MC no.442/2019.
Hence, claimants are held entitled for total compensation of `18,97,600/- in this case also.
Point no.(iii) answered accordingly.

Consequently, following :
ORDER i) MFA no.201928/2022 and MFA no.201929/2022 filed by insurer are allowed in part.
ii) Award modified to extent of holding insurer liable to pay compensation to claimants in first instance and thereafter recover it from insured without recourse to separate proceedings.
iii) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.
iv) MFA CROB no.200001/2023 and MFA CROB no.200002/2023 are allowed in part.
v) Claimants in both cross-objections are held  entitled for total compensation of  `18,97,600/- with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
- 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 vi) Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within a period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
vii) Direction issued by Tribunal regarding deposit and release shall apply to enhanced compensation also proportionately.

Sd/-

opennyai_summary.facts:
Separate claim petitions were filed by legal representatives of deceased against owner and insurer of light goods vehicle under Section 166 of Motor vehicles Act.
Owner though served did not file objection.
Insurer opposed claim petition on all counts.
Contributory negligence against rider of motorcycle and violation of terms and condition of policy by insured were also alleged.
On consideration, Tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of light goods vehicle by its driver, vehicle was insured with insurer and therefore insurer was liable to pay compensation.
It assessed compensation at `12,99,000/- with interest at 6% per annum and held insurer liable to pay same.
It was further submitted that Tribunal erred in not adding future prospects and even award under conventional heads was not in accordance with decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and others1 and sought for enhancement of compensation.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Therefore, points that arise for consideration in these appeals/cross objections are - "i) Whether Tribunal was justified in holding entire negligence against driver and insured light goods vehicle ?
ii) Whether Tribunal committed error in fastening liability upon insurer when there was violation of condition of policy ?
iii) Whether cross-objectors / claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for ?"
- 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 8.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Complaint is registered against driver of insured light goods vehicle for offences under Sections 279, 338 and 304A of Indian Penal Code read with Section 187 of Motor Vehicles Act.
The certificate was issued on 19.07.2019.
The accident occurred on 13.12.2018.
There is no reference in certificate about vehicle being subsequently certified fit.
Non-possession of fitness certificate would be in violation of terms and conditions of policy.
However, claimants in instant case are riders of motorcycle i.e., third parties, insofar as insurer herein is concerned.
Therefore, as held by Division Bench of this - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 Court in Mr.Rajesh Poojary v/s Mr.Rajesh2 and Full Bench in case of New India Assurance Company Limited v/s Yallavva and another3, non-possession of fitness certificate would not be a fundamental breach of terms and conditions of policy.
Therefore, insurer would be liable to pay compensation to claimants in first instance and thereafter recover same from insured.
opennyai_summary.decision:
For want of specific evidence regarding dependency, Tribunal deducted 50% towards personal expenses and applied multiplier of '18' and considered monthly income at `11,750/-.
Hence, claimants are held entitled for total compensation of `18,97,600/- in this case also.
Point no.(iii) answered accordingly.
Consequently, following :
ORDER i) MFA no.201928/2022 and MFA no.201929/2022 filed by insurer are allowed in part.
ii) Award modified to extent of holding insurer liable to pay compensation to claimants in first instance and thereafter recover it from insured without recourse to separate proceedings.
iii) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.
iv) MFA CROB no.200001/2023 and MFA CROB no.200002/2023 are allowed in part.
v) Claimants in both cross-objections are held  entitled for total compensation of  `18,97,600/- with interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
- 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:6435 vi) Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within a period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
vii) Direction issued by Tribunal regarding deposit and release shall apply to enhanced compensation also proportionately.
